params.body:
# Customer mode: one price, computed where it is shown

## Why

The price a customer sees was assembled in two places at once. `StockListController` computed the
customer price for the **first 20 vehicles of the current result page** when customer mode was
switched on, stored those amounts in the session under `stocklist_client_mode_prices`, and every
screen read that stored amount **before** reaching a formula. Only a vehicle outside those twenty
(page 2, another filter, a shared link, an expired session) fell through to the screen's own
arithmetic, and that arithmetic differed per screen.

Two things went wrong with that, both seen on staging:

* **The price froze.** When the selling dealer changed his trade price, the customer kept seeing
  the old amount until customer mode was switched off and on.
* **The vloot split in two.** The same vehicle was priced differently depending on whether it
  happened to be among the first twenty results.

It also hid the fact that the screens disagreed at all, which is why X-77 read as "five screens
compute differently" while in normal use they all showed the stored list price.

## What the session cache did, and what replaces it

Removed: the loop in `StockListController::client_vehicle_index_mode` that looked up twenty
vehicles and computed a price for each, the session key `stocklist_client_mode_prices`, and every
read of it (`hasPerVehiclePrice()` / `perVehiclePrice()` and the blade condition on the detail
page).

The session now carries **inputs only**: is customer mode on, which margin, with or without
damage, and one price per vehicle that the dealer **typed himself** in the customer-mode modal
(R S5-4.6, a real feature and a real input). That typed price moved to its own key,
`stocklist_client_mode_typed_prices`, so no key in the session can ever again hold a derived
amount. The margin modal now stores the margin and the damage choice and nothing else, which also
removes a stocklist query from that request.

## What is unified

One rule, in `App\Support\CustomerModePrice`, computed at the moment a screen shows it:

> **customer price = the trade price in the viewer's VAT + the viewer's margin**

No VAT on the margin, and no VAT on a margin vehicle at all. The trade price is expressed in the
rate of whoever is looking, which is the only VAT step there is: for a signed-in dealer that is the
existing accessor `trade_price_incl_dealer_vat` (it converts only when the two dealers' rates
differ), for a public page `CustomerModePrice::tradeInViewerVat()` does the same conversion with
the website dealer's rate.

It applies on the grid card, the classic index card, the detail page buybox, the offer and order
modals, the lease blocks, the dealer's public website (blade, API and the SQL twin in
`PublicWebsitePrice`) and the showroom slide.

This closes **X-77** and **X-74**, and it removes the detail page's VAT step on a margin vehicle.
Confirmed with Shane and the client on 2026-09-14: VAT is never added to a margin vehicle, and the
customer price is what you pay your colleague plus your own margin.

## What still differs per screen, and why

Only decisions about **which** price is shown, never about how it is computed:

* customer mode off: the dealer price, as always (R S5-4.3);
* the viewer's own vehicle: its retail price, and the card recomputes that to the viewer's VAT
  while the detail page and the lease block show it as entered (R S5-4.5);
* a sold vehicle on the detail page: its sold price (new rule R S5-4.12);
* the offer and order modals keep their looser reading of "customer mode on" and their lack of an
  ownership check, and fall back to the price already saved on the document;
* a new order on an own vehicle starts from the retail price;
* the website shows nothing ("op aanvraag") without a margin setting, the showroom slide shows the
  trade price in that case.

**The three readings of "customer mode on" are kept** (`=== 'true'`, `has && != 'false'`, key
present). They give the same answer for an absent key and for `'true'`; they differ only for a
session that still carries `client_mode = 'false'` together with a leftover margin, and such a
session exists in the wild (the margin modal never cleared the margin on `false`). Retiring them is
a separate, provable change, not one to make the day before the cutover.

## Behaviour changes, with amounts

Margin 500, both dealers at 21% VAT. "Before" is split where the stored price and the fallback
formula gave different numbers.

**VAT vehicle, trade price 10.000 incl.**

| Screen | Before (normal use) | Before (page 2 / expired session) | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grid card, index card | 10.605 | 10.605 | **10.500** |
| Detail page buybox | 10.605 | 10.605 | **10.500** |
| Offer and order modal, lease block | 10.605 | 10.500 | **10.500** |
| Dealer website, public API, price filter | 10.605 | n/a | **10.500** |
| Website lease calculator | 10.500 | n/a | 10.500 |
| Showroom slide | 10.605 | n/a | **10.500** |

**Margin vehicle, trade price 8.000**

| Screen | Before (normal use) | Before (page 2 / expired session) | After |
|---|---|---|---|
| Grid card, index card | 8.500 | 8.500 | 8.500 |
| Detail page buybox | 8.500 | 10.285 | **8.500** |
| Offer and order modal, lease block | 8.500 | 8.500 | 8.500 |
| Dealer website, public API | 8.500 | n/a | 8.500 |
| Showroom slide (X-74, margin added twice) | 9.000 | n/a | **8.500** |

Cross-border, unchanged in shape: a colleague in a country at 6% with a trade price of 10.600 incl.
is 10.000 excl., which is 12.100 at the viewer's 21%, so the customer sees 12.600.

In short: for a VAT vehicle the customer price drops by the VAT on the margin (105 in this
example), for a margin vehicle nothing changes except two defects that are now gone.

## Checked

* `CustomerModePriceTest` rewritten around the one rule: the rule itself, the VAT conversion
  including the cross-border case, one case asserting that all ten call sites give the same amount
  for a VAT vehicle and a margin vehicle, and the exceptions each in their own case with the
  numbers that changed noted in the docblock.
* New `CustomerModeSessionPriceTest` (feature): the margin modal stores inputs and no amounts, a
  changed trade price reaches the customer without touching the session, a vehicle "on page two"
  prices the same as one on page one, an amount planted under the old key has no effect on any
  screen, a typed price is kept and wins, switching the mode off wipes the inputs.
* Mutation-checked: reading the old session key again, restoring the detail page's VAT branch,
  storing a computed amount in the controller again and disabling the typed price each make the
  matching case fail.
* `PublicVehicleApiTest` updated deliberately: the VAT vehicle on a dealer website goes from 11.815
  to 11.500 with a margin of 1.500, for the same reason.
* `php artisan view:cache` plus `php -l` over all 418 compiled views.
* Full suite on a private MySQL database loaded as CI does. One unrelated failure in the worktree,
  `BuildStampTest` (404 on the build stamp because the worktree shares the main checkout's
  `public/build`); CI builds the assets itself.
* `docs/bedrijfsregels/`: S5-4 now states the rule, the exceptions, where it applies, a worked
  example table and what was removed and why; S5-4.4 rewritten, S5-4.1/3/5/6/7 adjusted, new
  R S5-4.11 (computed where it is shown) and R S5-4.12 (sold price); S2-5.12 and S2-7.6 point at
  the one rule; X-74 and X-77 moved to "Opgelost" with the amounts; V-10 in the acceptance test and
  the question sheet for Ilse turned into a confirmation. `92-testdekking.md` and
  `bedrijfsregels.html` regenerated (S5 coverage 28% to 40%).
